variants.title: Night scriptorium
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one high-fidelity visual concept for a medieval fantasy adventure journal in Foundry VTT. This is a flat, straight-on digital journal page, portrait composition about 1440 by 1800 pixels. Fill the image with the designed page. No physical book, desk, device, perspective, presentation-board captions, or browser chrome. The aesthetic should evoke an illuminated medieval manuscript while working as a modern readable interface.
Legibility is essential: a clear central reading column, roughly 60–70 characters per line, generous line spacing, large regular-weight serif body text, strong contrast. Use beautiful display lettering for titles only. Confine illustration, pigment texture and ornament to margins, separators, and section framing; keep text backgrounds calm. Use mixed-case headings. Highlight feature names through weight and color. Use restrained ornament with an intentional hierarchy. Do not use a colored vertical bar beside a paragraph, oversized quotation marks, modern rounded dashboard cards, or decoration over text.
Include a small atmospheric top-down image of a ruined dark-timber hunting lodge in a bare-birch clearing, and a compact cast row with four small circular painted portraits/icons labeled exactly "Ankou", "Shadow Doubles", "Felgo", "Treasure". These should remain subordinate to the prose.
Use this exact journal content, with careful readable spelling, and no other prose:
Title: "The Shadowless Lodge"
Metadata: "Investigation · Low threat · Level 16"
Heading: "Background"
Body: "The lodge belonged to a baron of the King's court. The King sent three pairs of scouts to use it as a forward post. The Fey Queen's ankou now waits here to measure the PCs. It carves away each victim's shadow and keeps the shadows as trophies."
Heading: "Arrival"
Read-aloud passage: "A lodge of dark timber sits in a clearing of bare birch, its antler-crowned gable sagging. On the threshold lies a man in royal green, face down, one hand reaching for the door. Every tree, stone and post casts a long shadow across the grass. The body casts none."
Heading: "Features"
Feature 1: "The threshold body. A royal scout, dead for two days with no wounds. DC 35 Medicine reveals that his heart simply stopped."
Feature 2: "Trophy wall. Five glass-eyed heads face the door. Something moved them without touching the ground."
Feature 3: "The shadow jar. Six slips of darkness flutter like moths. Opening the jar releases the stolen shadows."
Heading: "Outcomes"
Outcome 1: "Ankou escaped. It reports to the Fey Queen and remembers the PCs."
Outcome 2: "Shadows released. The scouts lie peacefully."

Art direction: NIGHT SCRIPTORIUM. A dark illuminated manuscript, charcoal-black ink ground, warm ivory text, antique gold fine lines, muted vermilion rubric headings and tiny lapis details. Precise, restrained Book of Kells interlacing. Symmetrical editorial composition. At the very top, a small gold interlaced emblem above the title. Under the title a shallow panoramic lodge vignette, then the compact cast row. Background begins with one modest illuminated gold initial. Arrival is the main focus: a hairline rectangular double frame with finely painted Celtic knot corners and a tiny centered knot flourish along the top, spacious inset text. Features and Outcomes remain open and airy, divided by small gold diamond ornaments. Leave substantial undecorated space. No continuous ornate outer border. This should feel like a precious night manuscript designed for effortless reading.

Art direction: BIRCH HERBARIUM. Pale warm vellum, nearly black brown text, deep moss-green headings, small iron-red rubric details. An organic illuminated manuscript informed by early medieval botanical marginalia. Asymmetric, airy composition: title upper left; a small square lodge illustration floats in the upper-right margin of the opening Background section, with the compact cast row immediately under the title. Main reading column remains a comfortable width. Two fine hand-painted birch twigs with tiny curling interlaced roots decorate diagonally opposite outer corners only. A tiny moth near the lower ornament echoes the shadow jar. Arrival has NO rectangular box: an elegant inset passage between two thin hand-drawn horizontal botanical dividers, with clean vellum around the text. Features use moss-green run-in leads and tiny leaf-shaped bullets. Outcomes sit under a small red rubric. Hand-painted detail, scholarly calm, ample white space, no artificial burnt edges, no texture behind prose. No continuous perimeter border.

Art direction: ROYAL FIELDBOOK. A formal medieval royal survey journal with a warm ivory page, deep oxblood rubric headings, dark ink prose, restrained indigo and antique gold. Architectural geometry and sober heraldic illumination; a small original crown-and-antler seal. Distinct layout: horizontal title masthead flanked by tiny knotwork terminals, seal to its right; beneath, a compact reference band places the square lodge map on the left and the four small cast portraits in an orderly row on the right. Background and the subsequent prose sections use one comfortable central reading column. Arrival has delicate stepped corner ornaments in oxblood and gold; most of the perimeter stays OPEN, without a full rectangle or any vertical side bar. Medieval carpet-page geometry appears only in small corner pieces and the masthead. Clean, tactile, precise, readable. Visually distinct from both a dark Celtic codex and an organic botanical page.
